fixes.explanation: Bethsaida it is, friend. Luke says Jesus took the apostles away privately and withdrew to a town called Bethsaida (Luke 9:10). The apostles are the Twelve, the men Jesus sent out earlier (Luke 6:13; 9:1, 2). Just a quiet getaway with His closest followers, and you know how well quiet worked out.

Capernaum is a town Jesus visits in Luke 4:31, so I see why it came to mind. But Luke 9:10 names a different place: Bethsaida. That's where Jesus withdrew with the apostles. Capernaum had a good run in Luke 4, but it's sitting this one out, friend.

HEAVEN is right, friend! Luke 9:16 says Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, spoke a blessing and broke them. Five loaves and two fish in front of about five thousand men (Luke 9:14), and the first thing He does is look up. Me? I'd be counting the dough three times and sweating through my apron.
